newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends relatively flat after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends relatively flat after quiet day.

text.p: * The Canada dollar ended relatively flat at C$1.3405
(US$0.7459) on Friday from Thursday's close at C$1.3410
(US$0.7457) after a lackluster session * Test of resistance at
C$1.3365 (US$0.7482) was easily rebuffed earlier in session
* Trading volumes were light as U.S. markets slowed ahead of
The currency has strengthened more than three Canadian cents from C$1.3757 (US$0.7269) on January 2, but some economists see a tougher road ahead for the Canadian dollar.
"As we approach C$1.33, there are several hurdles standing in the way of further progress," CIBC Wood Gundy senior economist Avery Shenfeld said in a report.

First, Shenfeld said he expected Canada's current account to show a deficit in the fourth quarter due to softer export data. That would follow two successive quarters of current account surpluses, which have been a factor behind the stronger dollar.
"Second, we're approaching territory for the (Canadian dollar) where chatter over further Bank of Canada rate cutting is bound to grow," Shenfeld said.
Finally, those investors that were surprised by the Canadian dollar's sell-off in November and December would not be caught unawares again, he said.
"Profit takers on Canada won't wait for the bounce off C$1.33 this time and should soon begin to cash in their chips on what has been a handsome...gain," Shenfeld said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2052 marks from 1.1895 marks and climbed to 87.44 yen from 86.90 yen.
